questions.topic: What is Angular and how it compares with React
questions.question: What is Angular, and how is it different from a JavaScript library such as React?

definition.text: Angular provides an integrated framework for building web applications.

motivation.whyIntroduced: Large web products need reusable UI composition, routing, forms, dependency management, template compilation and consistent conventions. Angular integrates these capabilities under one maintained framework.
motivation.historicalNote: Angular is a TypeScript-centric web framework; React primarily provides a component rendering library and an ecosystem of companion solutions. Both can build sophisticated applications.

problemSolved.before: Teams assemble unrelated UI, routing and state tools, and must establish conventions across packages themselves.
problemSolved.after: Angular supplies a cohesive application model, integrated compiler and first-party routing, forms, HTTP and dependency injection.

characteristics: Component-based rendering with templates and TypeScript classes
Official dependency injection, routing and form tooling
Reactive views with Signals and RxJS integration
Standalone components for composition and application bootstrapping
Angular CLI and AOT compilation tooling

simpleAnalogy.title: A complete workshop versus a box of tools
simpleAnalogy.explanation: A framework resembles a well-equipped workshop with standard workstations and established processes. A UI library provides a key workstation; teams choose the remaining equipment. Neither approach guarantees quality by itself.

industryExample.scenario: A banking portal needs account views, transfers, navigation, protected API access and consistent error handling.
industryExample.implementation: Build standalone components for account pages, the Angular Router for screens, injected services for API access and reactive forms for transfer input.
industryExample.businessImpact: Provides a predictable foundation across multiple frontend teams and features.
industryExample.importantConstraint: Angular does not automatically make payments secure: backend authorization, idempotency and financial rules remain server responsibilities.

useCases: Public applications needing coordinated routing and forms
Long-lived apps developed by multiple teams

steps: Browser loads index.html and JavaScript bundles
Bootstrap creates the Angular application and root component
Root template renders child components and routing outlet
User navigates to accounts or transfers
Component calls an injected service that contacts an authorized backend
Angular updates the UI when state changes

pitfalls: Angular and React are not equivalent batteries-included packages
Angular templates and decorators are compiled; they are not merely runtime string interpolation
Frontend route guards do not replace server authorization
Large apps still require disciplined architecture and dependency choices
whenNotToUse: Do not introduce a large Angular stack for an isolated static HTML fragment without meaningful application needs
Do not assume framework choice alone fixes poor data models or security
Do not force full client-side rendering where a static page meets requirements more simply

alternatives.tradeoff: More architecture decisions and integration responsibilities

alternatives.bestFor: Small static widgets or content-focused pages

Standalone root component bootstraps without an NgModule

questions.question: What are the major building blocks of an Angular application?

definition.text: Angular applications combine components, templates, services, routing and reactivity.

motivation.whyIntroduced: As web UIs evolve, mixing every interaction, API call and rendering rule in one file becomes difficult to test. Angular establishes composable UI and dependency boundaries.
motivation.historicalNote: Building blocks include framework-level elements such as directives and pipes and application features like routing and reactive forms. Some are optional depending on the application.

problemSolved.before: A monolithic script both renders the page, handles clicks and makes requests, coupling unrelated responsibilities.
problemSolved.after: Components own views, services encapsulate shared behavior, injectors provide dependencies, and the router selects feature screens.

characteristics: Components contain a template, selector and class behavior
Templates bind values and events; directives change template behavior
Pipes format display values without modifying source data
Services and injectors share logic with defined lifetimes
Router, forms, HttpClient and Signals support navigation, input, networking and reactivity

simpleAnalogy.title: Departments in a well-run library
simpleAnalogy.explanation: A library has a public desk, catalog, checkout desk, and supporting staff. Each has a specific responsibility, but they cooperate to serve the visitor. Components handle presentation while services provide reusable operations.

industryExample.scenario: A shopping portal displays product lists, prices, cart state and checkout screens.
industryExample.implementation: Use ProductCard and CartSummary components, CurrencyPipe for prices, a CartService for shared cart behavior, and the router for catalog/checkout screens.
industryExample.businessImpact: A new feature can reuse product views or cart logic without duplicating their implementations.
industryExample.importantConstraint: Display totals are not authoritative order prices; the backend must calculate final price, taxes, discounts and inventory.

useCases: Centralize shared cart behavior in a service
Format prices and dates with pipes
Track reactive totals with computed Signals

steps: Root component renders catalog screen
Catalog component receives a list of typed products
Template iterates product cards with stable tracking keys
Product card emits Add click to its parent
Cart service updates state and derived total
Template displays the new total; checkout verifies price server-side

 B --> C[Product card components]
 C -->|Add event| B
 B --> D[Cart service]
 D --> E[Cart Signal state]
 E --> F[Computed cart total]
 F --> G[Cart summary component]
 G --> H[Backend checkout validation]

explanation: CartService is injectable and owns a writable private Signal
The component reads a derived, read-only computed total
Dependency injection supplies the same root-scoped service to consumers
Cart total is a local preview, not the authoritative checkout amount
A full production cart would merge existing items by ID and verify product availability

projectExperience.example: In an e-commerce learning app, I would separate product components from a cart service and derive preview totals without duplicating calculations in each component.

pitfalls: A root-level mutable service can accidentally retain unrelated user sessions if not reset on logout
Pipes should not perform costly side effects
Directives and components are not interchangeable
A frontend computed cart total can be stale or manipulated
whenNotToUse: Do not put all business logic directly in templates
Do not make every component a globally shared service
Do not treat a UI price calculation as proof of what a customer owes

alternatives.bestFor: State used by only one component subtree
alternatives.tradeoff: Not automatically shared across unrelated routes

alternatives.bestFor: Large cross-feature event-driven state with tooling needs
alternatives.tradeoff: Extra concepts and boilerplate for simple applications

testing.strategy: Write focused service and component tests; check that a derived value updates without direct mutation.

testCases.expected: Total equals sum of each minor-unit price times quantity

negativeCases: Negative quantity and invalid prices should be rejected by domain validation
Never use browser total as backend checkout authority

questions.question: What is an Angular component, and what does the @Component decorator do?

definition.text: An Angular component binds a class to rendered markup.

motivation.whyIntroduced: Reusable screens need localized behavior and a declarative description of their rendered view. Angular component metadata allows the compiler to connect selectors, templates, styles and dependencies to a class.
motivation.historicalNote: The @Component decorator marks the class as a component and carries configuration metadata used by Angular compilation and runtime behavior. The class itself is ordinary TypeScript.

problemSolved.before: Developers hand-write DOM manipulation and have no explicit reusable unit describing the view and its behavior.
problemSolved.after: A decorated class defines a reusable, independently testable element with a template, selector and optional imports and styles.

characteristics: A selector identifies where the component host is instantiated
A template expresses UI with bindings and events
The TypeScript class exposes state and event handlers
The metadata imports array lists template dependencies for standalone components
Styles can be component-scoped using Angular view encapsulation

simpleAnalogy.title: A recipe card for a reusable dish
simpleAnalogy.explanation: The class is the cook who performs actions; the template is the plated presentation; the decorator describes the dish, where to serve it and the tools it needs.

industryExample.scenario: An appointment portal displays each booked appointment and offers a cancel action.
industryExample.implementation: Create an AppointmentCard component with an input appointment model, a template and an output cancellation event.
industryExample.businessImpact: The same appointment card can be reused in a patient view and clinician worklist without duplicating the presentation.
industryExample.importantConstraint: The cancel event only signals user intent; the backend must authorize and confirm the appointment cancellation.

steps: Parent receives authorized appointment list
Parent renders one appointment card per item
Angular supplies appointment input to child
Child template displays status and button
Click emits appointment ID to parent
Parent sends authorized cancellation request and refreshes state

codeExample.runtime: Angular 20+ standalone application; Angular CLI + strict TypeScript + browser runtime. Files shown with // FILE: markers.
explanation: The @Component metadata defines the selector and HTML template
The required signal input exposes typed appointment data
output<string>() emits an event to the parent when clicked
The parent handles intent without claiming that cancellation succeeded
In a real app the parent would call an authorized API and handle pending/errors

projectExperience.example: For a healthcare appointment learning feature, I would reuse a typed appointment card and emit cancellation requests rather than having the child perform direct database changes.
evidenceToCollect: Component test asserting output event payload
API test proving unauthorized cancellation is rejected
projectExperience.doNotClaim: Use conditional language until implemented and tested; do not claim production delivery without evidence.

pitfalls: Required input must be provided or template checking fails
Output events are not global event buses
Selectors must be valid and imported components declared in parent imports
Component styling encapsulation is not a security boundary
Avoid displaying sensitive details in logs or unprotected UI
whenNotToUse: Do not turn every tiny markup span into a separate component without reuse or responsibility
Do not call APIs directly in the template
Do not treat a component event as confirmed server-side success

alternatives.tradeoff: Does not define a full view like a component

questions.question: What is the difference between standalone components and NgModules?

definition.text: Standalone components declare dependencies without requiring NgModule declarations.

motivation.whyIntroduced: Earlier Angular applications organized declarables using NgModule declarations and imports. Standalone APIs reduce indirection and let components express template dependencies directly.
motivation.historicalNote: Standalone components became available in Angular 14 and are the modern default. Components in older applications can still use standalone: false and belong to an NgModule; these styles can interoperate during migration.

problemSolved.before: A component must be declared in an NgModule to participate in that module system and its template dependencies are scoped through module imports.
problemSolved.after: A standalone component can import its own template dependencies directly and can be bootstrapped or lazy loaded through modern application APIs.

characteristics: Standalone components import their template dependencies in @Component metadata
NgModule-declared components require a module declaration
Providers can be configured at root, route or component scope in either architecture
Modern Angular defaults to standalone; older versions before 19 did not
Migration can be incremental and coexist with legacy modules

simpleAnalogy.title: Each room has its own equipment list
simpleAnalogy.explanation: NgModules resemble departments that maintain centralized equipment lists. Standalone components carry their own approved tool list, making dependencies visible where they are used. Shared services still need explicit scope management.

industryExample.scenario: An enterprise SaaS app is migrating an old administrator module to individually lazy-loaded features.
industryExample.implementation: Keep the legacy NgModule working while new feature screens use standalone components with local imports and route-level providers.
industryExample.businessImpact: Teams can migrate route by route and reduce accidental shared-module coupling.
industryExample.importantConstraint: Converting to standalone does not by itself reduce bundle size, enforce tenancy or guarantee performance; verify actual builds and route isolation.

steps: User navigates to workspace settings
Router loads standalone settings component
Component imports its local directives and child components
Router resolves providers scoped to settings route
Component requests tenant-aware service
Backend independently validates tenant access

A component with standalone:false cannot be directly imported as a standalone component

Do not import NgModule-declared components directly into standalone imports; import their declaring module

alternatives.tradeoff: Requires consistent imports and scope conventions

questions.topic: Create an Angular application with routed features
questions.question: How would you create a standalone Angular application with a navigation header, dashboard and account-details component?

definition.text: Bootstrap a standalone shell, then configure reusable routed views.

motivation.whyIntroduced: A multi-screen portal needs one persistent navigation shell but independently addressable pages. Routing decouples browser URLs from component instantiation and allows direct links and lazy loading.
motivation.historicalNote: Angular CLI generates application scaffolding; bootstrapApplication and provideRouter configure a standalone root. The RouterOutlet renders whichever route matches the current URL.

problemSolved.before: An app switches views using manual DOM mutations or deeply nested conditional flags, breaking deep links, browser history and clear screen ownership.
problemSolved.after: A persistent shell displays navigation while RouterOutlet selects the dashboard or account details by route.

characteristics: bootstrapApplication starts a standalone root component
provideRouter registers declarative routes and guards when needed
RouterLink creates navigation without page reload
RouterOutlet hosts the selected route component
Route parameters identify a selected account; backend must authorize the ID

simpleAnalogy.title: Building with hallways and rooms
simpleAnalogy.explanation: The navigation header is the hallway shared by everyone. A route is the room number; the router opens the selected room without reconstructing the entire building.

industryExample.scenario: A fictional banking portal has an overview and a shareable URL for each account details page.
industryExample.implementation: Use a root navigation header, dashboard component and account-details route /accounts/:accountId; read the route parameter and display fictional data.
industryExample.businessImpact: Users can open account URLs directly and keep a consistent navigation experience.
industryExample.importantConstraint: A route parameter is untrusted input: a real backend must verify ownership before returning account data. Never infer authorization from an ID in a URL.

steps: Browser loads root index.html and compiled bundles
main.ts bootstraps AppComponent and provides router
AppComponent renders header and router outlet
Dashboard route shows overview
User follows routerLink to /accounts/demo-001
AccountDetails reads accountId from the route
Real service would query backend and server would authorize account access

explanation: Root component stays mounted while RouterOutlet changes the active view
Both feature screens are standalone and loaded through dynamic imports
RouterLink performs internal navigation and supports browser history
The route snapshot works for this navigation example; if the same component instance remains active while parameters change, subscribe to paramMap or convert it to a Signal
There is deliberately no real bank account lookup or authentication in this beginner demo

projectExperience.example: For a banking portfolio project, I would implement this shell first, then wire account details to a backend endpoint and enforce authorization before displaying customer records.

Browser screenshot of the dashboard and account detail URLs
E2E test proving direct route refresh works

pitfalls: A snapshot parameter does not track later param changes in the same component instance
Router guards can be bypassed or disabled on the client
Unknown URLs need a deliberate fallback or not-found page
Screen content should include meaningful landmarks and headings
Lazy routes still require sensible chunk size and error handling
whenNotToUse: Do not fetch sensitive account data based solely on an unverified route ID
Do not hardcode credentials or secrets into frontend files
Do not choose a route snapshot if parameters must update without component recreation

alternatives.name: Eager route component
alternatives.bestFor: Tiny critical routes that do not need a lazy chunk
alternatives.tradeoff: Adds code to the initial bundle

alternatives.name: Manual component conditional rendering
alternatives.bestFor: Small UI mode switches inside one route
alternatives.tradeoff: Does not provide URL-based navigation or history

Server fallback supports reloading /accounts/demo-001 and Angular shows the details component

negativeCases: A production account endpoint must return 403 or 404 when the requester lacks authorization
If web server is not configured with SPA fallback, deep links may return a server-side 404
